result.proposed_fix: In _separator_word, restore the script-agnostic rule before any stripping: `if all(unicodedata.category(ch)[0] == 'M' for ch in w[2]): return True`, then apply base=_bare(w[2]) for words that have a base letter. More robust: in _words, treat category-M characters that do not follow a base letter as gap characters, so mark-only words are never produced. Add regression cases (as \u escapes, self-contained): 'refunds-portal \u093c\u0901\u0902 shop', '\u0f39\u0f37\u0f35 shop', '\u0650\u065c\u0655 shop', '\u0e31\u0e34\u0e47 shop', '\u0c3c\u0c00\u0c01 shop', '\u093c\u0901\u0902\u0903 cash'. Assert has_link_or_contact is True and mask_links removes 'refunds-portal'. Keep the R19 and R20 cases passing.
result.root_cause: uri_web/untrusted.py _words() counts any category-M character as a letter (_letter, line 449-450), so a run of marks with no base letter after a space becomes a 'word' tagged with the marks' own script. Commit 68feb3e7 changed _separator_word (line 580-582) to classify base=_bare(w[2]) and treat the word as a separator only if base is empty or one letter. _bare (line 472-476) removes only marks whose Unicode name starts with 'COMBINING', so script marks (U+093C DEVANAGARI SIGN NUKTA, U+0901/0902, U+0F39/0F37/0F35, U+0650/065C/0655, U+0E31/0E34/0E47, U+0C3C/0C00/0C01) stay in base. base then has 3 distinct characters (more than _MAX_FOREIGN=2), its script differs from the TLD's and it is not in _STROKES, so the mark run is taken as the NAME. The gap before 'shop' is a plain space and 'shop' is not in _CORE, so line 614 drops the match. has_link_or_contact returns False and mask_links, verify, extractive, the surface and the A2UI check all let it through.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: eb4d676d (R19-01) added a correct, script-agnostic rule: all(unicodedata.category(ch)[0]=='M' for ch in w[2]) returns True. Its tests (tests/web/test_w1_closure_r19_review_regressions.py:16-17) only used marks named 'COMBINING ...' (U+0323/0307/0308/0304), copied from the reviewer's probe. 68feb3e7 (R20-01) replaced that rule with `not base` after _bare(), which narrowed 'all category M' to 'all named COMBINING'. The R19 tests still passed, so the regression was not caught. Both repairs targeted the reviewer's exact characters, not the cause: _words makes words out of marks that have no base letter. The earlier repairs ca622bc0..fe77015a predate the mark-only word case.
